_README: Base output filters shipped with ClaudeKit. Consumed by
Do NOT edit this file to add project-specific filters: create
.claude/operations/scripts/output-filters.local.json with the same shape. Entries there
override these by `id`, and because that file never ships with the kit it never appears
in .claudekit-manifest.json, which is what makes preserve_assets.py keep it across an
so it is refused unless the filter also sets "lossy": true). Placeholders available in
lossy too: it keeps a head and a tail around a marker naming the omitted byte count.
Scope is measured, not guessed. Over 4,355 Bash calls in .claude/hooks/hooks.log across
12 active days, the pytest progress lines are 97% of the strippable bytes; git status
and gen-plan-index.py --check together are 3%, and their lines carry filenames rather
than noise. One filter, therefore, not sixty-four.

filters.description: Drop pytest -q progress lines whose every mark is a pass or a skip. A full suite here is 11,282 tests at a measured 1.147 bytes per mark = 12,940 bytes of dots per green run. A line containing F, E, x, X or u does not match this pattern and survives untouched, so a removed line provably carried no failure.
filters.summary: [ck output-filter: pytest-progress] {removed} all-passing progress line(s) removed ({marks} pass/skip markers). Prefix the command with CK_RAW_OUTPUT=1 for raw output.

filters.description: Last-resort byte cap on Bash stdout. Measured: planner runs slurp single tool results of 38-66K chars, and one 401K-context planner run spent most of its budget on them. select() returns the FIRST matching filter and load_filters preserves base-file order, so this entry MUST stay LAST: a command with a specific filter (pytest-progress) keeps that filter and is not capped. NEVER_FILTER commands are refused before any filter is consulted.
filters.summary: [ck output-filter: {id}] stdout capped; see the inline marker for details.
